text:
maria: heads up — eu-central1 nvme read latency jumped, GPUs failing to attach. seeing attach errors in scheduler logs. ?

sre-bot: ALERT: nodepool/eu-central1-nvme had 90th p99 read latency 320ms over last 5m. affected: gpu-attach, batch-provisioning.

alex: looking at node logs — I see a filesystem rekey/re-encrypt job kicked off around the same time after a KMS rotation. `fscrypt` spawn on many scratch mounts.

jamal: who rotated keys? that could explain coordinated heavy reads.

kevin: we rotated keys last night during the low window; assume the rekey job is background re-encrypt that scans local devices. it should be low-priority but looks like it's saturating reads.

maria: sample from /var/log/syslog on gnode-211:
```
Mar 23 02:12:09 gnode-211 fscrypt[4129]: rekey job started for /scratch (device /dev/nvme0n1p1)
Mar 23 02:12:11 kernel: nvme 0000:3b:00.0: read latency: 76ms -> 398ms
Mar 23 02:12:41 kubelet: attach failed: ProvisionTimeout
```

alex: nice catch. that explains p99. two approaches: pause rekey jobs cluster-wide (if safe), or throttle their IO priority.

jamal: can we pause? is re-encryption mandatory immediately?

kevin: it's not urgent. keys rotated to be ready for rotation window, re-encrypt was scheduled by policy. we can pause and schedule low-io re-encrypt windows.

maria: proposed mitigation steps: 1) add io.weight cap for fscrypt processes (systemd slice) 2) pause remaining rekey jobs via controller 3) route new gpu attaches away from eu-central1 temporarily.

alex: commands I ran to throttle current jobs (tested on one node):
```bash
# lower blkio throttle for pid 4129
eqosctl blkio set 4129 --rw-iops=500 --rw-bps=50M
# or systemd slice override to CPUWeight/IOWeight
sudo systemctl set-property fscrypt.service IOWeight=10
```

jamal: can we patch the controller to pause the rekey rollout? which service did that?

kevin: it's a cron in key-ops service — I just paused the rollout in key-ops (confirmed). still need to kill in-flight jobs gracefully.

maria: killing in-flight fscrypt workers on all affected nodes now (SIGTERM then SIGKILL if not exit). also bumped attachment fallback to other regions for 15m while we stabilize.

sre-bot: ACTION: paused key-ops rekey rollout (by kevin). nodes with rekey workers signalled (maria). routing policy updated: prefer-region us-west2 for new gpu attaches for 15m.

alex: after throttling/killing, p99 read back down to ~28ms on sampled node. attach retries succeeding.

maria: status: GPU attach backlog cleared for the queue we were watching. rekey jobs will be rescheduled with io caps and staged during off-peak.

kevin: cost note — routing to us-west2 added ~+12% egress/latency cost for the short window, but prevented SLA violations. we should add a preflight: detect scheduled heavy local IO after key ops changes.

jamal: agreed. recommendation: add an interlock between key rotation and re-encrypt start — only start re-encrypt when fleet IO headroom > threshold. file a follow-up.

maria: filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-7893 "kms-triggered re-encrypt -> IO headroom interlock + throttles" with mitigation steps and cost estimate.

kevin: 👍 also include rollback play for quick pause + route policy flip.

maria: thanks all — keeping eyes on eu-central1, will post updates if anything regresses :white_check_mark:
file_comment: kms rekey triggered fscrypt causing NVMe read latency spike and GPU attach failures; thread documents mitigation and follow-ups
